label: checker-a
statement: Reviewed all 40 sampled typed tools across all eight batches using only classifier-contract.md and checker-a-sample.json; no quarantine file was read. No sampled tool contains an optional analog.

findings.issue: Bounded retention substitutes a remedy for the named unbounded replay anti-pattern.
findings.reason: Finite history-limit models bounded replay, not the named absence of a buffer limit.

judgments.reason: Named seek, avoidance and separation weights change combined acceleration and the selected units' trajectories.
Separation, cohesion and velocity-match weights alter flock spacing, centroid movement and heading variance.
Steering ranks and an acceleration threshold select the active significant steering group, changing movement and switches.
Seek precedes wander; the acceleration threshold makes the fallback activate near equilibrium and changes stalled steps.
Slot spacing changes fixed slot positions and formation width for the selected squad, with measurable slot error.
Travel, danger and visibility costs reweight selected regions and can change the chosen route and route cost.
Source strength and radius change the influence field around selected units and the resulting control frontier.
A distance-decay exponent changes influence falloff, while source strength changes its magnitude and reach.
The influence radius changes the field boundary and the number of terrain regions affected by selected sources.
A terrain cost multiplier reweights edges through selected regions and can divert unit routes.
Anchor speed moves the formation reference while slot spacing sets subordinate positions, changing trajectories and formation error.
Distance, danger and exposure weights change edge costs and the routes selected from those costs.
A numeric selector threshold admits or drops whole unit messages, visibly changing delivery counts.
Recipient count controls copies routed to a numbered receiving set, changing deliveries and copy count.
The next sequence number gates release from a bounded reorder buffer, making consecutive delivery observable.
The send window caps unacknowledged progress, changing outstanding messages and sender blocking time.
Pool size and per-performer capacity route received work to available performers, changing listener blocking and backlog.
The type count defines numbered type-specific routes; message type determines its receiving channel and mismatch count.
The stated reciprocal creator-created relation supplies a closed path across levels; loop depth controls its visible traversal.
Description level switches visible rule steps and whole-system detail, directly changing the displayed level.
The stated capture-display feedback supplies a real representation loop; loop depth changes its visible traversal.
The stated code-to-editor return supplies a closed cross-level path; loop depth changes how much of it is exposed.
Description level changes which nested conversation, narrator or viewer frame is displayed.
Magnification level changes visible symbol groupings and therefore the displayed level of description.
Await-reply mode and in-flight capacity change whether senders wait while unit messages and replies are delivered.
Batch size and flush interval change when queued command messages are released together and their waiting time.
Subscriber count and notification delay change which units receive notifications and when delivery occurs.
A single active input with completion-gated succession serializes queued inputs and preserves their message order.
Active-input capacity permits concurrent routes and queues excess inputs, changing interleaving and delivery latency.
The stated first-emitter routing rule retains one winning input and closes competing routes, changing cancellations.
The delivery limit passes the first configured number of messages and then closes the route.
One active input plus continue-after-error advances queued inputs on completion or failure while suppressing failure forwarding.
A silence timeout switches delivery to the designated fallback input, changing timeout and fallback delivery counts.
A finite history limit and bounded suffix implement bounded replay, contradicting the named absence of a buffer size.
The duplicate-suppression flag filters adjacent equal accepted payloads while changed payloads continue.
The accepted numeric message type changes which unit messages are routed and which are rejected.
A single in-flight delivery and drop-while-busy policy discard arrivals until acknowledgement frees the route.
A time window and message limit flush queued messages as batches; the empty-batch flag suppresses empty deliveries.
Forming a squad from 7–9 selected units implements the size limit as visible squad membership and size.
Messages per tick limits admissions on the selected channel, changing delivery throughput and queued backlog.
